entities.summary: Gérard de Ridefort, also called Gerard de Ridefort, was Grand Master of the Knights Templar from the end of 1184 and until his death in 1189. During his tenure, the Knights Templar underwent significant organizational changes, including the implementation of a new military strategy and the establishment of a more centralized leadership structure. The Templars also expanded their influence and control over the Holy Land, capturing the strategic fortress of Safed in 1189. De Ridefort's leadership during this period was marked by a strong sense of devotion to the Templar Order and a commitment to its ideals of chivalry and military service. He was succeeded by Everard des Barres, who would go on to lead the Templars through the tumultuous years of the 13th century. De Ridefort's legacy as Grand Master of the Knights Templar has endured for centuries, with his name becoming synonymous with the Order's bravery and martial prowess. The historian and chronicler, Jean de Joinville, praised de Ridefort's leadership, stating that he was "a man of great virtue and a just leader." De Ridefort's own writings, which have been lost to time, are believed to have been preserved by his successors, offering valuable insights into the inner workings of the Templar Order during this period. The influence of de Ridefort's leadership can be seen in the many Templar castles and fortifications that were built during his tenure, including the famous stronghold of Belfort, which he himself besieged in 1189.
